topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its interdisciplinary audience, and the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer development as a disruption of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how accumulated genetic and epigenetic alterations disrupt normal developmental differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Histological hallmarks of tumor invasion and metastatic progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the pathological progression of tumors from encapsulated benign lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies across different organ systems.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the standard conventions for naming neoplasms and the physiological mechanisms through which tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human populations and multicellular organisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine epidemiological patterns of cancer in humans alongside comparative oncology across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale, histological detection methods, and diagnostic limitations of screening for pre-malignant and early-stage tumors.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes and practical session reminders.
